title: Claude helps label decisions, blind: a model's labels kept apart from a person's
request: The owner asked to use Claude Sonnet for labelling the blind decisions, and to get help from Claude models for labelling.
spec: A model sees exactly the blind view of each drawn decision and answers it; its labels are their own source, named and weighted, never the effective label, never exported as a person's, and a gap when it cannot tell.
plan: Read the label contract, its consumers and the blind draw.
Add a model source in a new contract version that reads old labels.
Write the labeller through a gateway purpose with its own prompt and a cap.
Keep its labels apart in the summary and the sets.

decisions.decision: A model's labels never become the effective label.
decisions.why: Agreement with a model is not correctness, and a model may itself be one of the answerers measured.

decisions.decision: A new contract version rather than reusing a source.
decisions.why: Filing a model's opinion as measured or blind would make it read as truth.

decisions.decision: The labeller has its own prompt and purpose, not the decision answerer's.
decisions.why: Labels from the same prompt as an answerer would grade that answerer by itself.

change: dclab_core/ledger.py (decision_label v2, the model source, weights on the draw), datasets.py, prompts/decision_labeler.md and HASHES, schemas (v2 baseline), CHANGELOG 0.37.0; dclab_rnd/ledger/model_labels.py (new), models/settings.py and agents/harness.py (the decision_labeler purpose); tests model_labels (new) and datasets; docs/guides/BLIND_LABELLING.md.

findings.defect: A model's label was refused for its evidence.
findings.scenario: No label was kept: the evidence kind was not one the contract knows.
findings.cause: A new kind was used without the contract.

findings.defect: A model's label was refused for its weight.
findings.scenario: Labels on the blind draw without their weight could not be estimated.
findings.cause: Only a person's blind label could carry a weight.
findings.fix: A label of the draw carries its weight, a person's or a model's.

findings.defect: The decision sets had no place for a model's label.
findings.scenario: A model label would be dropped from the set or mixed with others.
findings.fix: A model column of its own, with its name.

findings.defect: Every stored label of the old version was lost or broke reads.
findings.scenario: A label written before the change vanished from the files and made the database's reads fail.
findings.cause: Reading checked the version before the upgrade could run.
findings.fix: A contract declares the older versions it reads; the data card's v1 too.

findings.defect: One model label broke the decision sets.
findings.scenario: Building the sets refused a model label whose name had been cut to its kind.
findings.cause: The export kept only a person's kind, and treated a model like a person.

findings.defect: The cap or a provider refusal ended the run with a traceback.
findings.scenario: A capped run printed no counts and no spend.
findings.fix: The run stops, keeps what it wrote and says why.

findings.defect: What the labeller may see understated project points.
findings.scenario: A project's id and its aggregate measures went unlisted on the Admin page.
findings.cause: The text named column points only.

findings.defect: A test checked keys the view never had.
findings.scenario: The blind view test could not fail.
findings.cause: It asserted absent keys of another shape.
findings.fix: It checks the view's keys are within the blind view's.

outcome: Claude can label the drawn decisions as a second opinion; the owner's labels stay the truth.
lessons: A model's label is a second opinion: give it a source of its own, never one that reads as truth.
A new contract version must be read through the same path stored documents take, and tested there.
risks: Claude's labels were not run on the owner's ledger yet: the dev database needs make dev's migration first.
